definitions.explanation: A soldier or armed guard stationed to protect a place such as a palace, gate, or important building. Often refers to the ceremonial guards at royal or government sites.

examples.japanese: {門|もん}の{前|まえ}に{衛兵|えいへい}が{立|た}っている。
examples.english: A guard is standing in front of the gate.

examples.japanese: {宮殿|きゅうでん}の{衛兵|えいへい}は{微動|びどう}だにしなかった。
examples.english: The palace guards did not move a muscle.

examples.japanese: {観光客|かんこうきゃく}は{衛兵|えいへい}の{交代|こうたい}を{見|み}ようと{広場|ひろば}に{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: Tourists gathered in the square to watch the changing of the guard.

notes:
Composed of {衛|えい} (to guard, defend) + {兵|へい} (soldier). Refers to a soldier posted to guard a location, often a ceremonial palace or government guard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {衛兵|えいへい}が{立|た}つ: for a guard to stand watch
- {衛兵|えいへい}の{交代|こうたい}: the changing of the guard
- {衛兵|えいへい}を{配置|はいち}する: to post sentries

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {番兵|ばんぺい}: sentry; guard on watch — emphasizes standing watch at a post
- {護衛|ごえい}: escort; bodyguard — protects a specific person while moving, not a fixed post
